items.title: Want to buy your kid an AI toy this Christmas? Not in New York
items.excerpt: New York has banned AI chatbot toys for five years as new research from Common Sense Media reveals troubling safety failures, including exposure to inappropriate content and risks to emotional development.

items.title: New York bans AI chatbot toys for kids.
items.excerpt:
Governor Kathy Hochul signed a bill putting a five-year pause on the manufacturing, distribution, and sale of AI chatbot toys, including “talking stuffed animals, dolls and robots that use the internet to hold conversations with kids.” This comes just one month after the state also restricted how chatbots could interact with minors.

items.title: After AI toys told kids disturbing things, New York is banning them for five years
items.excerpt: New York has banned the manufacture and sale of AI chatbot toys for five years, following California. The law covers talking plushies, dolls and robots, takes effect 90 days after the November 24 signing, and carries fines of up to $15,000 a day.

items.title: Child safety groups across the world are begging Amazon to remove AI toys for kids
items.excerpt: A plush bunny marketed for ages 3 and up reportedly connects to chatbots whose own terms say 13 and older.

items.title: $799 Smart Glasses Promise Vision Pro-Style Controls in a 45g Frame
items.excerpt: Hong Kong startup Savage Technology has announced its first product, "Orrorin Glasses," promising Vision Pro-style pinch controls and full-color displays for both eyes in a frame weighing just 45 grams. The company describes the glasses as offering "Vision Pro–level interaction" and being around 25 times lighter than Apple's headset, including its external battery.

items.title: AI Toys Are a Nightmare Before Christmas
items.excerpt: AI-powered toys marketed as companions for young children remain on shelves this holiday season as New York Gov. Kathy Hochul signs a five-year ban on making and selling AI toys for young kids ($15,000 per violation), following California's September moratorium.

items.excerpt: Looking at Plaud One and Nothing's upcoming Ear (note), Gizmodo argues earbuds are a natural home for AI assistants and notetakers, but misheard commands and hallucinated answers make the AI itself the weak link.
